purpose: rapidcsv is a header-only C++ CSV parser library.

functions.rapidcsv::Document::InsertColumn: Inserts a new column at `pColumnIdx` in the document. If `pColumn` is empty, it creates a blank column sized to current data rows; otherwise it converts values to strings and places them starting after the header row (`mLabelParams.mColumnNameIdx + 1`). `pColumnName` sets the column label.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumn: `GetColumn` reads one CSV column as `std::vector<T>`, by zero-based index or header name, with optional converter. It skips label rows, converts each cell, and throws `std::out_of_range` if a row lacks that column. Example: `doc.GetColumn<float>("Close")`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowCount: `GetRowCount()` returns the number of data rows, excluding any label/header rows. Use it to query how many rows are available for row-based access. It computes `mData.size() - (mLabelParams.mColumnNameIdx + 1)` and returns `0` if that would be negative.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnCount: Returns the number of data columns, excluding row-label columns. It uses the first data row (or `mColumnNameIdx` if set) and subtracts `mRowNameIdx+1`. If there’s no data or the result is negative, it returns 0.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnNames: `GetColumnNames()` returns the CSV’s column labels from the header row, or `{}` if no column-name row is configured/available. Use it to inspect/exist-check names (e.g. `find`). No special caveats noted.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetCell: `GetCell` retrieves one CSV cell by row/column index or label, converting it to `T` via standard conversion (or a custom `ConvFunc`). Use zero-based indices; label overloads need matching headers. Examples show reading string/numeric values. No special caveats noted beyond `char` using the cell’s first byte.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter::ToStr: `ToStr()` is the value→CSV-string converter in `rapidcsv::Converter`. Use/override it to customize serialization; docs show specializing `Converter<int>` (example overrides `ToVal()`, and README says `ToStr()` can also be overridden). It formats ints/chars directly, float/double with setprecision.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowNames: `GetRowNames()` returns all row labels from a CSV when `LabelParams` defines a row-name column. It skips data before the header row. Use it like `GetColumnNames()` to check names. If no row-name index is set, it returns an empty vector.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnIdx: Returns the zero-based data-column index for a named header. Use it only when column labels are enabled and names are unique. If the name is missing or labels aren’t set, it returns -1. Duplicate names make the result undefined.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetColumnName: Returns the header/name for a zero-based data column. Use it only when `mLabelParams.mColumnNameIdx >= 0`; otherwise it throws `std::out_of_range`. It maps the requested column through `GetDataColumnIndex()` and reads that cell from the column-name row.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Load: Load sets the Document’s path/parse params then reads CSV via `ReadCsv()`. Use it with a file path or binary `istream`; defaults are provided. Docs show file, stream/stringstream, and comment-line skipping examples.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Clear: `Clear()` resets a `rapidcsv::Document` to an empty state: it removes all loaded data, column names, and row names, and resets encoding flags (`mIsUtf16`, `mIsLE`, `mHasUtf8BOM`) to false. Use it when you want to reuse the same `Document` object for new data.
functions.rapidcsv::no_converter::what: `rapidcsv::no_converter::what()` is the exception message accessor for failed/unsupported type conversion. Use it via `catch(const std::exception&)` or `catch(const rapidcsv::no_converter&)` to get `"unsupported conversion datatype"`. It always returns that fixed string.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetRow: `SetRow` writes a row into the CSV by zero-based data row index or by row name. It auto-expands missing rows/columns as needed, converts values to strings, and stores them starting after the row-name column. If the row is shorter, existing cells beyond it are left unchanged.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetColumn: `SetColumn` writes a whole column into the CSV by index or name. It auto-expands rows/columns if needed, converts values to strings, and stores them starting after the header row/label offset. Use it with a vector matching the desired column data; missing space is created, existing cells are overwritten.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::InsertRow: Design: insert a data row at zero-based `pRowIdx` in the document. Use `pRow` to fill cells; `pRowName` is the row label. If `pRow` is empty, it creates a row sized to current column count. If `pRowIdx` is past the end, it pads with empty rows before inserting.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowIdx: Returns the zero-based data row index for a row label. Use it after row labels are enabled; it looks up `pRowName` in `mRowNames` and adjusts for column-name rows. Returns `-1` if not found/labels disabled. Duplicate row names are undefined.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRowName: Returns the row label for a zero-based data row index. Use it only when `mLabelParams.mRowNameIdx >= 0`; otherwise it throws `std::out_of_range`. It maps the row index via `GetDataRowIndex()` and then returns that cell from `mData`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetCell: `SetCell` writes a value into the CSV at a chosen cell. Use any overload by column/row index or names. If the target row/column doesn’t exist, it expands `mData` to fit, then converts `pCell` to string and stores it.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter<std::basic_string<ch: `ToStr` is the default value→string converter for `Converter<T>`. Use/override it for custom serialization. It formats ints/char via `ostringstream`, float with precision 9, double 17. Docs show overriding `ToVal`/`ToStr` and mention test035.cpp; no cautions noted.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetColumnName: `SetColumnName` assigns a header name to a zero-based data column. It requires `mColumnNameIdx >= 0` or throws `out_of_range`. It updates the name map, removes any old name, and resizes the table/row as needed so the name can be stored.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::RemoveColumn: Removes a column by zero-based index (or name via overload). It maps to the data-column index, erases that element from each data row, and throws `std::out_of_range` if the column is missing on a row. Then it updates column names.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter<std::basic_string<ch: Aim: convert CSV text to a numeric T. Use via rapidcsv’s default converter or specialize `Converter<T>::ToVal()` to override/add conversions. It parses ints/longs/etc., with range checks for small integer types and throws on invalid/out-of-range input. Example: README ex008.cpp; also test035.cpp.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::SetRowName: Sets the row-label string for a zero-based data row and updates the internal name→row map. Requires a valid row-name column index; if `mRowNameIdx < 0`, it throws `std::out_of_range`. It also resizes the table/row if needed and replaces any old name.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::Save: `Document::Save` writes the current CSV data out. Use `Save(path)` to save to a new/updated file path; if `path` is empty, it uses the document’s existing path. The stream overload writes to a provided `ostream`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::GetRow: `GetRow` returns a row as `std::vector<T>`, by row name or zero-based index, with optional conversion. If the named row isn’t found, it throws `std::out_of_range`. Example: `doc.GetRow<std::string>("2017-02-22")`.
functions.rapidcsv::Document::RemoveRow: Removes a row from the CSV document by zero-based data-row index or by row label. If the index maps past `mData.size()`, it throws `std::out_of_range`. After removal, row names are updated.
functions.rapidcsv::Converter::ToVal: `ToVal()` converts a CSV string to numeric `T` for `Converter`/`GetColumn<T>()` etc. Use by specializing/overriding it for custom types or behavior. It parses ints/longs/etc., checks range for small ints, and may throw on bad/out-of-range input. Example: `Converter<int>::ToVal()` in README; also refs `test035.cpp`.
